metaDescription: Azawakh vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Azawakh boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Colostrum fade is the clock behind this Azawakh table, and doses at 8, 12, 16, 16 weeks exist to immunize the puppy while exposure (parks, foster homes, boarding intros) is rising.
Boarding desks ask for finished Azawakh dates, not intentions, so a Azawakh with only the first DA2PP / DHPP dose is still incomplete for most facilities.
Hypothyroidism shows up often enough in Azawakhs that vaccine day is also screening day — keep both on the same visit when possible.
Store the rabies label with the Azawakh profile immediately; lost paperwork is the most common reason Azawakh travel and kennel check-ins stall.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: If your Azawakh misses the dose scheduled near week 12, call the clinic the same day with product names — do not restart the Azawakh series from memory.
The danger for a delayed Azawakh is the gap, not the embarrassment, because parvovirus pressure stays real for an under-vaccinated puppy even in clean-looking neighborhoods.
While waiting for the make-up DA2PP / DHPP visit, skip high-traffic dog parks / unknown-cat intros and keep the Azawakh away from unvaccinated animals.
After catch-up, rewrite reminders for the next Azawakh due date (7, 3, and 1 day prior) so the same miss does not recur.

faqs.question: When does the Azawakh core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Azawakh misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Azawakh health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Azawakh adult health guide for breed predispositions such as hypothyroidism, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
